From 8d7ba71e46216b8657a82ca2ec118bc93812a4d0 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Kery Qi <qikeyu2017@gmail.com>
Date: Sat, 24 Jan 2026 05:10:31 +0800
Subject: [PATCH] rocker: fix memory leak in rocker_world_port_post_fini()

In rocker_world_port_pre_init(), rocker_port->wpriv is allocated with
kzalloc(wops->port_priv_size, GFP_KERNEL). However, in
rocker_world_port_post_fini(), the memory is only freed when
wops->port_post_fini callback is set:

    if (!wops->port_post_fini)
        return;
    wops->port_post_fini(rocker_port);
    kfree(rocker_port->wpriv);

Since rocker_ofdpa_ops does not implement port_post_fini callback
(it is NULL), the wpriv memory allocated for each port is never freed
when ports are removed. This leads to a memory leak of
sizeof(struct ofdpa_port) bytes per port on every device removal.

Fix this by always calling kfree(rocker_port->wpriv) regardless of
whether the port_post_fini callback exists.

Fixes: e420114eef4a ("rocker: introduce worlds infrastructure")
Signed-off-by: Kery Qi <qikeyu2017@gmail.com>
Reviewed-by: Simon Horman <horms@kernel.org>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260123211030.2109-2-qikeyu2017@gmail.com
Signed-off-by: Jakub Kicinski <kuba@kernel.org>

diff --git a/drivers/net/ethernet/rocker/rocker_main.c b/drivers/net/ethernet/rocker/rocker_main.c
index 36af94a2e062..2794f75df8fc 100644
--- a/drivers/net/ethernet/rocker/rocker_main.c
+++ b/drivers/net/ethernet/rocker/rocker_main.c
@@ -1524,9 +1524,8 @@ static void rocker_world_port_post_fini(struct rocker_port *rocker_port)
 {
 	struct rocker_world_ops *wops = rocker_port->rocker->wops;
 
-	if (!wops->port_post_fini)
-		return;
-	wops->port_post_fini(rocker_port);
+	if (wops->port_post_fini)
+		wops->port_post_fini(rocker_port);
 	kfree(rocker_port->wpriv);
 }
 
-- 
2.34.1

The patch fixes a memory leak in the `rocker` driver's `rocker_world_port_post_fini` function.

### Modifications in `drivers/net/ethernet/rocker/rocker_main.c`:
- In the function `rocker_world_port_post_fini`, the condition is reversed: instead of returning early if `wops->port_post_fini` is `NULL`, now the callback is called **only if it is set**, and the memory `rocker_port->wpriv` is **always freed** via `kfree()` after the (optional) callback.

### Relationship between modifications:
- The single-file change is self-contained. Previously, when `port_post_fini` was `NULL` (as in the `rocker_ofdpa_ops`), the function would return immediately without freeing the `wpriv` memory allocated in `rocker_world_port_pre_init`. The fix ensures that `kfree(rocker_port->wpriv)` is always executed, regardless of whether the world-specific post-finalize callback exists, thereby resolving the memory leak for ports without such a callback.

Here is the commit message:
rocker: fix memory leak in rocker_world_port_post_fini()

In rocker_world_port_pre_init(), rocker_port->wpriv is allocated with
kzalloc(wops->port_priv_size, GFP_KERNEL). However, in
rocker_world_port_post_fini(), the memory is only freed when
wops->port_post_fini callback is set:

    if (!wops->port_post_fini)
        return;
    wops->port_post_fini(rocker_port);
    kfree(rocker_port->wpriv);

Since rocker_ofdpa_ops does not implement port_post_fini callback
(it is NULL), the wpriv memory allocated for each port is never freed
when ports are removed. This leads to a memory leak of
sizeof(struct ofdpa_port) bytes per port on every device removal.

Fix this by always calling kfree(rocker_port->wpriv) regardless of
whether the port_post_fini callback exists.

Fixes: e420114eef4a ("rocker: introduce worlds infrastructure")
Signed-off-by: Kery Qi <qikeyu2017@gmail.com>
Reviewed-by: Simon Horman <horms@kernel.org>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260123211030.2109-2-qikeyu2017@gmail.com
Signed-off-by: Jakub Kicinski <kuba@kernel.org>

Here is the root cause:
In `rocker_world_port_post_fini()`, the memory allocated for `rocker_port->wpriv` was only freed after calling the world-specific `port_post_fini` callback. However, if the callback was not implemented (e.g., `rocker_ofdpa_ops` has `port_post_fini` set to NULL), the function returned early without freeing the memory, causing a leak of `sizeof(struct ofdpa_port)` per port on removal.

Here is the patch:
 
 static void rocker_world_port_post_fini(struct rocker_port *rocker_port)
 {
 	struct rocker_world_ops *wops = rocker_port->rocker->wops;
 
-	if (!wops->port_post_fini)
-		return;
-	wops->port_post_fini(rocker_port);
+	if (wops->port_post_fini)
+		wops->port_post_fini(rocker_port);
 	kfree(rocker_port->wpriv);
 }

Root cause:
In `rocker_world_port_post_fini()`, the memory allocated for `rocker_port->wpriv` was only freed after calling the world-specific `port_post_fini` callback. However, if the callback was not implemented (e.g., `rocker_ofdpa_ops` has `port_post_fini` set to NULL), the function returned early without freeing the memory, causing a leak of `sizeof(struct ofdpa_port)` per port on removal.

Code statements information:
The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```
if (!wops->port_post_fini)
    return;
wops->port_post_fini(rocker_port);
```
Reason:
When `wops->port_post_fini` is `NULL`, the function returns early before reaching the `kfree(rocker_port->wpriv)` that follows. This skips the deallocation of the memory allocated in `rocker_world_port_pre_init()`, causing a memory leak.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```
if (wops->port_post_fini)
    wops->port_post_fini(rocker_port);
kfree(rocker_port->wpriv);
```
Reason:
By wrapping the callback call in a conditional, the function now always executes `kfree(rocker_port->wpriv)` regardless of whether the callback exists. This ensures the per‑port private memory is freed on every port removal, eliminating the leak.
